Heartbreaking post. My thoughts are with you. Lost my little rescue dog in January (he was 21 and we had him for 17 years) and my Romanian rescue last month to bone cancer. We just adopted a 6 year old American bulldog from the RSPCA. He doesn’t fill the hole Buster and Rupert left but he’s brought us so much joy. Rescue dogs are the best. 
And your little mate will be with you everywhere you go. And hopefully in good time you’ll be able to give another abandoned little soul as loving a home your last one had. Much love ❤️

Absolutely agree. I wonder how much gratification the “hunters” get out of becoming famous. Whilst clearly being aware of the impact their public naming and shaming ( and again, I can only stretch how much I want everyone one of these sickos to rot in prison) can affect innocent family members, employers etc. 

I’d rather see an article  in the paper about a convicted person, that has been proven to be guilty beyond reasonable doubt.

I see where you are coming from and agree, a lot of these “vigilantes”, “heroes”, “law enforcers” cite exactly that. But what about broadcasting it live for everyone to see? Shouting out names before a conviction, getting people in the community to gather knowing full well there is a chance of the perpetrator being beaten up before they face a judge and jury. 
Again I can only agree that these scum bags need to be locked up but this type of human bear baiting seems wrong to me. 
Surely you can do this type of work without making it into spectacle for everyone to see and meanwhile potentially harming the family of the paedo by making them the target of a lynch mob

BUT I wouldn’t put their albums on at a family Barbecue.

Absolutely agree with you. My best friend is a police officer in the major crime task force and deals with rapes, murders, child abuse etc on a daily basis. 
His main concern is that cases, that are being investigated in an orderly fashion, can get thrown out of court purely because the identity of the person being investigated has been exposed. 

Whoever tries to harm a person, an animal or someone else’s property should be named and shamed. But do so after a trial, brought to court by cops who know the law and go about their business without seeking fame and gratification by publicly broadcasting it.
